paper.abstract_en: The Standard Model Higgs potential seems unstable at field values $h > h_{\rm top} \sim 10^{10}$ GeV. Vacuum decay can be triggered by $N\sim 4π/λ\sim 1000$ overlapped Higgs bosons with energy $\sqrtλ h_{\rm top}$. However, this configuration is stimulated by ultra-high energy collisions with a $\exp(-{\cal O}(N))$ suppression, comparable to spontaneous vacuum decay: no `Higgspolosion' enhancement arises. This implies that ultra-high energy cosmic ray collisions are safe, despite that their number (in production sites) likely is tens of orders of magnitude higher than what usually estimated (in space). We speculate on how vacuum decay could be induced classically at futuristic ultra-high energy colliders (either using a few right-handed electron beams, or a double collision producing an in-coming wave of $N$ boosted Higgs bosons) and on how the resulting vacuum bubble could be controlled to extract energy.
